summary: The compact one-room gabled form is recognizable and pleasantly simplified, but the dominant wall and roof treatments do not match the reference studio and weaken its identity.

orientation.summary: The model has one principal door on +u, the southeast-facing end (145°), and a window on +v, the southwest wall (235°). This agrees with the geolocated SV1 oblique view, which faces both +u and +v and shows the small stepped entry on the southeast end with the white-trimmed window on the southwest side. The four-face sheet and actual inventory confirm a single +u portal, with no duplicate principal entrance.

issues.problem: The walls read as red brick, while the reference shows reddish-brown timber/shingle cladding—a characteristic part of the camp-studio appearance.
issues.fix: Replace the brick pattern with simplified reddish-brown wood shingles or horizontal timber siding.

issues.problem: The roof is rendered as gray rectangular shingles, whereas the reference roof is pale, lightly ribbed sheet metal with clean projecting eaves.
issues.fix: Use a pale cream or light-gray metal roof with subtle parallel seams and retain the shallow gable and overhangs.

issues.problem: The open door appears as an unusually thick bright-white slab and distracts from the otherwise restrained miniature.
issues.fix: Simplify it to a thin muted door and frame, preferably shown closed or only slightly ajar above the small steps.
